Between the Prophet's house and his pulpit is a garden of the gardens of Paradise, and his pulpit is on his fountain tank.
Medina is a sanctuary between its two mountains, its trees and game protected and innovators cursed; the Prophet built his mosque, called it Tabah, and said it expels bad people.
People will leave Medina though it is better for them; faith returns to it like a snake to its hole, its plotters dissolve, and afflictions will fall among its houses.
Medina expels bad people as fire cleans iron, the Prophet said when a bedouin asked to cancel his pledge and when believers split over hypocrites who turned back from Uhud.
The Prophet asked double Mecca's blessings for Medina, hastened on seeing its walls, kept Bani Salama at home, and said a garden of Paradise lies between his house and pulpit.
When Abu Bakr and Bilal caught Medina's fever, the Prophet prayed Medina be loved like Mecca or more and its fever moved away; Umar asked for martyrdom and death there.
Seeing Uhud, the Prophet says it loves us and we love it, and declares the area between Medina's two mountains a sanctuary, as Abraham made Mecca one.
After the emigration Abu Bakr and Bilal had fever, and the Prophet asked Allah to make Medina loved as Mecca or more, healthy and blessed, moving its fever to Al-Juhfa.
The Prophet asked Allah to make them love Medina as much as Mecca or more, move its fever to Al-Juhfa, and bless their measures.
Medina is a sanctuary whose trees may not be cut, and whoever innovates a heresy or sins there incurs the curse of Allah, the angels and all people.
A bedouin refused release from his pledge left Medina, which expels impurities like bellows, and Umar delayed a sermon until Medina, place of the Sunna and the companions.
The Prophet said Uhud loves us and is loved by us, made Medina a sanctuary as Abraham did Mecca, and between his house and pulpit is a garden of Paradise.
Umar and Uthman were heard preaching from the Prophet's pulpit.
The Prophet allied the Ansar and Quraish in Anas's house at Medina; Abdullah bin Salam let a visitor drink from the Prophet's bowl and pray in his mosque.
Angels guard Medina, and if Allah wills neither the Dajjal nor plague will come near it.
